description: Orchestration, seed corpus & QA — a job runner that drives many categories end-to-end (acquire -> normalize -> link -> export) with scheduling, incremental re-runs, a catalog, and quality gates, then proves the whole system by building a real multi-domain seed corpus (dishes, sculptures, monuments, battles, languages) and validating the resulting graph.

userStories.title: Define a pipeline job model and config
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to declare an end-to-end job so categories run reproducibly through every stage.
acceptanceCriteria: Define a Job config (one or more category specs, target stages: acquire/normalize/link/export, output paths)
Jobs are declared in a jobs/<name>.yml and validated on load with clear errors
A Job dataclass exposes the ordered stages to run
Tests pass (pytest) loading valid and invalid job configs
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement the pipeline runner
userStories.description: As a user, I want a single runner that chains acquire -> normalize -> link -> export so I don't wire stages by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: Runner executes the stages from US-001 in order, passing each stage's output dir to the next, calling the modules from Tasklists 1-5
A stage failure stops that job with a clear error and a non-zero exit, leaving completed stage outputs intact
Per-stage timing and row counts are recorded
Tests pass (pytest) running a fixture job end-to-end with adapters mocked
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement incremental / idempotent re-runs
userStories.description: As a user, I want re-running a job to update only what changed so large corpora are cheap to refresh.
acceptanceCriteria: Each stage records an input fingerprint; a stage is skipped when inputs are unchanged unless --force is given
Re-running an unchanged job performs no network calls and reports 'up to date'
Updated source data triggers re-normalization and re-linking only for affected categories
Tests pass (pytest) asserting a second run is a no-op and a changed input triggers re-processing
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Run categories concurrently with backpressure
userStories.description: As a user, I want many categories processed in parallel within polite limits so large corpora finish quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: Acquire stages for independent categories run concurrently up to a configurable worker cap
Per-host rate limits from the acquisition client are respected across concurrent workers
A failure in one category does not abort the others; a final summary lists per-category status
Tests pass (pytest) running multiple fixture categories concurrently with a stubbed adapter
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Build a dataset catalog
userStories.description: As a user, I want an index of every category and its stats so the corpus is discoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: Maintain catalog.json listing each category: id, label, source, node/edge counts, dimensions covered, last run timestamp, provenance summary
Catalog is regenerated/updated after each job run
Provide `culturescrape catalog` to print the catalog as a table
Tests pass (pytest) asserting catalog entries match a fixture run
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Implement quality gates
userStories.description: As a user, I want automated QA so low-quality scrapes are flagged before they pollute the graph.
acceptanceCriteria: Gates check: minimum row count vs expected, max duplicate rate post-dedup, provenance completeness, dangling-edge rate, and unreconciled-entity rate
Each gate has a configurable threshold; violations are reported and (optionally) fail the run
A QA report (JSON + printed summary) is written per job
Tests pass (pytest) for a passing fixture and a fixture that trips each gate
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Author the seed-corpus job specs
userStories.description: As a user, I want real multi-domain categories defined so the system is exercised on actual data.
acceptanceCriteria: Add jobs/seed-corpus.yml referencing category specs for at least: Peruvian dishes, Italian sculptures, German architectural monuments, American Civil War battles, and a language-family dataset
Each category specifies its source (wikidata-sparql/petscan/dump), dimensions, and link types
All seed category specs validate against the loaders
Tests pass (pytest) validating every seed category and the job spec load
Lint passes (ruff)

userStories.title: Run the seed corpus and produce graph + exports
userStories.description: As a user, I want the seed corpus actually built so I have a real dataset and proof the pipeline works end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: Running the seed-corpus job produces canonical TSV (nodes + edges), passes schema validation, and passes the quality gates
Generate the Neo4j import script and the Datalog (.pl/.dl) exports for the seed corpus
Connectivity metrics show the seed corpus is one largely-connected component (largest component above a documented threshold)
Tests pass (pytest) on a recorded/fixture-backed subset so the run is reproducible offline in CI
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add a top-level run CLI and unify the command surface
userStories.description: As a user, I want one entrypoint to run jobs so the whole system is operable from the command line.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `culturescrape run <job.yml> [--stages ...] [--force] [--workers N]` orchestrating everything
`culturescrape --help` lists all subcommands (fetch, normalize, link, to-neo4j, from-neo4j, to-datalog, run, catalog, validate)
Running the seed job via the CLI reproduces the US-008 outputs
Tests pass (pytest) invoking `run` on a fixture job
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Add scheduled refresh support
userStories.description: As a user, I want corpora refreshed on a schedule so data stays current without manual runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Provide a `culturescrape run --since <duration>` mode plus a documented cron/systemd-timer example invoking it
Scheduled runs use incremental mode (US-003) so unchanged categories are skipped
A run log records what was refreshed and what was skipped
Tests pass (pytest) asserting the --since flag selects only stale categories on a fixture catalog
Type checks pass (mypy)

userStories.title: Write the end-to-end documentation and quickstart
userStories.description: As a new user, I want a quickstart so I can go from zero to a queryable graph.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/quickstart.md walks through: install, define a category, run the pipeline, import to Neo4j, export to Datalog, and run an example query
README.md links the quickstart, the six tasklists, PLAN.md, and the data model
All commands in the quickstart are covered by a smoke test on the fixture corpus
Tests pass (pytest) for the quickstart smoke test
Lint passes (ruff)
